thread.title: Venezuelan Delivery Driver Shot by ICE Agent in Austin Undergoes Surgery to Remove Bullet

author: Mynorthwest
title: Venezuelan Delivery Driver Shot by ICE Agent in Austin Undergoes Surgery to Remove Bullet
text:
Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a Venezuelan delivery driver shot by a federal immigration agent in Austin, had surgery to remove a bullet lodged in his back for nearly two weeks.
Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan delivery driver, underwent surgery Thursday to remove a bullet lodged in his back for nearly two weeks after he was shot by a federal immigration agent in Austin, Texas. The shooting occurred on Sept. 20, when Garces Perez was pulled over while delivering food for DoorDash. He remains in custody on charges that he assaulted an officer while trying to evade arrest.
Shooting and Aftermath in Austin
Garces Perez had appeared in court on Wednesday in a wheelchair, wearing a sling on his arm. According to authorities, he struck an officer with his side mirror on Sept. 20 while trying to drive away. The federal officer who shot Garces Perez, and who allegedly was hit by the side mirror of Garces Perez car, was not wearing a body camera.
Fabiana Melendez Ruiz, a spokesperson for his legal team, said the bullet was successfully removed during surgery, and Garces Perez is recovering in the custody of the U.S. Marshals. His case has sparked outrage and protests in the Texas capital city against President Donald Trump immigration crackdown, including agents conduct.
Garces Perez said he was struck by a law enforcement SUV and spun around before he was shot. Federal officers told investigators, however, that Garces Perez attempted to strike an officer with his car at the end of the chase before the officer fired his weapon. Footage provided Wednesday in court shows officers pulling over Garces Perez in Austin, where he was delivering food for DoorDash.
Protests Erupt Over Immigration Enforcement
Demonstrators gathered in response to the shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a Venezuelan man who was shot in his vehicle by an ICE officer the previous day in Austin, Texas, on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026. The protests reflect growing tensions over federal immigration enforcement tactics and the conduct of agents during arrests.
The incident has drawn attention to the use of force by immigration officers and the lack of body camera footage in such encounters. Community members and advocates have called for greater accountability and transparency in how immigration laws are enforced.
National Immigration Debates Intensify
With early voting already underway, a question worrying some voters is what role, if any, immigration enforcement officers might have at polling places through Election Day. Department of Homeland Security officials say they do not plan to send immigration enforcement officers en masse to patrol the polls and dismissed concerns that such a deployment could intimidate voters.
The Democratic National Committee on Thursday filed a lawsuit alleging that President Donald Trump administration secretly changed a postcard used by U.S. citizens overseas in a way that makes it harder to register to vote. The lawsuit contends that the Department of Defense made the change by declaring an emergency, which allowed it to eliminate certain steps.
These developments come amid a broader national debate over immigration policies and their impact on communities. The shooting of Garces Perez has become a flashpoint in that debate, highlighting the human consequences of enforcement actions.
Energy Costs and Other News
Households in the contiguous United States will pay thousands of dollars more for energy through 2040 because of federal policy changes since President Donald Trump returned to office, according to modeling released Friday by a nonpartisan think tank. The Energy Innovation analysis found that households will pay an average of $6,500 more for energy, cumulatively.
In other news, Secretary of State Marco Rubio has waived a restriction on $320 million in military aid to Egypt that had been previously withheld over human rights concerns, citing Egypt help in dealing with Iran since the conflict began earlier this year. The State Department said Thursday that Rubio had signed off on the waiver.
An Arizona man 10-year manslaughter sentence has been tossed in a case where a video generated by artificial intelligence portrayed the deceased victim addressing a judge before the punishment was imposed. In a decision released Wednesday, the Arizona Court of Appeals concluded Gabriel Paul Horcasitas must be resentenced in the 2021 shooting.
Meanwhile, a 10-year trial measuring outcomes of over 300 patients treated with CyberKnife across 21 centers has shown promising results for prostate cancer treatment. June is National Men Health Month, and one in eight men will hear the words you have prostate cancer in their lifetime, making preventative care crucial.
